title: AI Engineering
blurb: Build products on LLMs: APIs, prompting, structured output, RAG, agents, evaluation and operations.

quiz.question: Why does a chatbot need the conversation history re-sent on every API call?
options: The API caches it but needs confirmation
LLM APIs are stateless; the model only sees what is in the current request
It is only required for streaming
quiz.explanation: Models are stateless; chat "memory" is the history you resend, which costs input tokens every call.

quiz.question: What is the most reliable way to get machine-readable output from an LLM?
options: Ask politely for JSON in the prompt
Use schema-enforced structured output or tool calling, then validate (e.g. Pydantic/Zod)
Parse the text with regular expressions
quiz.explanation: Schema-constrained output plus validation (and re-asking on failure) removes parse failures.

quiz.question: In a RAG system, a user asks about "order o_4821" and retrieval misses the right document. What most likely helps?
options: Hybrid search that combines keyword (BM25) and vector retrieval
quiz.explanation: Exact identifiers are matched far better by keyword search; hybrid retrieval combines both.

quiz.question: Where must permission checks for RAG documents be enforced?
options: In the retrieval query filter, before content reaches the model
quiz.explanation: Prompts cannot enforce access control; filter by access level at retrieval time.

quiz.question: What is the primary defence against prompt injection in an agent that can send emails?
options: Least-privilege, user-scoped tools plus human approval for irreversible actions
quiz.explanation: Security must come from the system: scoped permissions, approvals, allow-lists and sandboxing.

quiz.question: What is a key pitfall of LLM-as-judge evaluation?
options: Position and verbosity bias, so rubrics and human calibration are needed
It is always slower than humans
quiz.explanation: Judges favour position, length and sometimes their own outputs; use anchored rubrics, pairwise randomised comparisons and calibration.

quiz.question: Which metric best reflects how fast a streamed LLM response feels to users?
quiz.explanation: Perceived speed is dominated by when the first tokens appear.

problems.title: Design a support RAG bot
problems.prompt: Design a RAG assistant over a help centre and order data for a delivery app. Cover ingestion, retrieval, generation, security and evaluation.
problems.solution: Ingest: parse, chunk by structure with metadata (url, updated, audience), embed, incremental re-index. Retrieve: hybrid BM25+vector with access filters, rerank top 30 to 5. Generate: grounded prompt with citations and refusal rule; order lookups via user-scoped tools. Operate: eval set with retrieval hit-rate and judged faithfulness in CI, tracing, cost/latency dashboards, injection tests.

problems.title: Cut LLM cost by 70%
problems.prompt: A summarisation feature costs too much. Propose and validate cost reductions.
problems.solution: Log tokens per request, trim context, cap max_tokens, enable prompt caching, route to a smaller model and verify quality on an eval set, cache identical requests, move non-urgent work to batch APIs; ship behind a canary watching quality metrics.
